issues.description: The template for the arbitrary-n QFT defines the forward-transform method as _qft_circuit_n_qubits (leading underscore), while both the problem statement (Exercise 7 tasks) and the solution use/expect qft_circuit_n_qubits (no leading underscore). This name mismatch is structural: students following the template will implement _qft_circuit_n_qubits, but tests or later code (and the provided solution) call qft_circuit_n_qubits, causing confusion and failing automated tests or reference runs.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the template method to match the problem statement and solution: change def _qft_circuit_n_qubits(self, qc: QuantumCircuit) to def qft_circuit_n_qubits(self, qc: QuantumCircuit). Ensure the inverse method (qft_circuit_n_qubits_inverse) calls/uses this same method name. This preserves the pedagogical intent while making the template, tests, and solution consistent.

issues.description: The problem statement (Exercise 7) and the solution implementation expect a public method named qft_circuit_n_qubits for the QFT on an arbitrary number of qubits, but the template repository defines the method with a leading underscore: _qft_circuit_n_qubits. This inconsistency in the method identifier (leading underscore vs. none) breaks the straightforward mapping from the exercise description/tests -> template -> solution. Students will be confused about which method to implement and tests or autograders that call qft_circuit_n_qubits will fail to find the implementation in the template.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the template method from _qft_circuit_n_qubits to qft_circuit_n_qubits (remove the leading underscore) so the template signature matches the problem statement/tests and the solution. Ensure any references (tests/autograders) use the same name.
